title: Aegis Event Schema v1
description: Locked contract between the sensing layer (C daemon, aegisd) and the policy layer (Python rule engine). Changes require explicit renegotiation between both teammates. Do not modify unilaterally mid-project.

event_id.description: UUID v4, generated by the sensing layer (C). Uniquely identifies this event instance. Generated using /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid or a simple UUID4 implementation in C.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of when the event was detected by the sensing layer. Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ

event_type.description: Discriminator field — determines which fields appear in the detail object. Policy layer must branch on this field first.

source.description: The process that caused or is associated with this event. Always present regardless of event_type.

pid.description: Process ID of the process associated with this event.

ppid.description: Parent process ID. 0 if no parent (kernel thread). Key field for lineage-based detection rules.

uid.description: Real user ID of the process. Read from /proc/[pid]/status (Uid field, first value).

euid.description: Effective user ID. Read from /proc/[pid]/status (Uid field, second value). euid=0 with uid!=0 is a key privilege escalation signal.

cmdline.description: Full command line of the process. Read from /proc/[pid]/cmdline (null-bytes replaced with spaces). May be empty for kernel threads.

exe_path.description: Resolved path of the executable. Read by readlink on /proc/[pid]/exe. May be '(deleted)' if the binary was removed after launch — itself a suspicious signal.

open_fds.description: Optional. Symlink targets of open file descriptors, read from /proc/[pid]/fd/. Include only when relevant to the event type (e.g., process_spawn anomaly detection). Arrays may be large — include deliberately, not by default.

detail.description: Event-type-specific payload. Structure depends entirely on event_type. See per-type definitions below.

parent_exe_path.description: Resolved exe path of the parent process (ppid). Enables lineage-based rules: e.g., shell spawned from web server.

parent_cmdline.description: Full command line of the parent process.

is_setuid.description: True if the spawned executable has the setuid bit set. Read from stat() on the exe_path.

exit_code.description: Exit code of the process. Non-zero exits from sensitive processes can be a detection signal.

duration_seconds.description: Optional. Time in seconds between process spawn and exit, if the spawn event was also tracked. Very short-lived processes spawned from unexpected parents are a detection signal.

local_addr.description: Local IP address. IPv4 only in v1. Decoded from hex in /proc/net/tcp.

remote_addr.description: Remote IP address. 0.0.0.0 for listening sockets.

remote_port.description: Remote port number. 0 for listening sockets.

state.description: TCP connection state, decoded from the hex state field in /proc/net/tcp.

protocol.description: Protocol. TCP only in v1. UDP and IPv6 are explicitly deferred.

path.description: Absolute path of the modified file. Must be in the configured watch list — Aegis does not watch all files, only a defined sensitive set.

old_hash.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the file contents at last known-good state.

new_hash.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the file contents at time of detection.

size_before.description: Optional. File size in bytes before modification.

size_after.description: Optional. File size in bytes after modification.

new_euid.description: Effective UID after the change. Transition to 0 is the primary privilege escalation signal.

trigger.description: Optional. What mechanism caused the change — setuid binary execution, or a direct UID change (e.g., via su/sudo). 'unknown' if the mechanism cannot be determined from /proc alone.
